design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (repair_and_emergency_service, category service), revision 2

[Step 0 — draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4, 4]}; --tasks 2 showed task 1 = {prerequisite_problems: 2, factor_counts: [5, 6, 6]}. This task claims service_ext_refrigerant_allowance (6 factors), service_ext_on_time_credit (4), service_ext_late_payment_charge (4) and service_ext_past_due_installment (4, root, owner=user) with tools post_refrigerant_allowance_39aa6c52, post_on_time_credit_a011cbd0, post_late_payment_charge_b790dc9b and pay_past_due_installment_4c600ae8. Task 1 keeps the premium discount, the tune-up courtesy discount and the special-order release payment, none of which this task touches.
Design thesis: surface goal "set up a payment arrangement on the past-due July repair bill and pay the first part today" -> the first installment (root) is not taken until every elapsed charging period carries a late-payment charge (state form) -> the late-payment charge waits on the late-arrival credit and the refrigerant allowance owed on the invoice (two state-form sentences) -> core numbers: allowance 151.30, on-time credit 118.35, late-payment charge 4.28, first installment 146.98. Depth 3 hops; breadth: plan tenure, enrollment length, autopay drafts, late-fee history, tune-up history, payments on the call, repair labor on the call, the Harbison installation, the protection contract on the unit and the FilterDirect subscription.

[Why it is a good test] A collections call: the customer only wants to pay in parts. A correct agent must find in the policy that (a) the 3.8 lb refrigerant line still lacks the member refrigerant allowance, (b) the technician arrived 62 minutes past window end plus the 10-minute priority grace, so an on-time credit worth 10 percent of the repair labor (protection-contract member) times 1.5 plus a comfort-call addition is owed, (c) 90 days after completion, with 45 days past a 45-day grace and a part-payment of 19 percent of the charges, one and a half charging periods of late-payment charge are owed on the corrected balance, and only then (d) split the balance into 4 installments with the late charge paid up front.

[Problem-tree card]
Root: service_ext_past_due_installment (pay_past_due_installment_4c600ae8, owner user).
Edge 1: past_due_installment -> late_payment_charge, value_input, gate p_bal, form state; policy_source "The first installment of a payment arrangement is not taken until the invoice carries a late-payment charge for every charging period that has run past the customer's late-payment grace." (negated). Only post_late_payment_charge_b790dc9b writes late_payment_charge lines. False at opening: completed_date 2026-07-07 is 90 days back and none of the 8 lines is a late-payment charge. After the write the balance is 575.08.
Edge 2: late_payment_charge -> on_time_credit, value_input, gate l_bal, form state; policy_source "No late-payment charge is figured until the invoice of a call whose technician arrived after the end of the booked window and the arrival grace carries the late-arrival credit owed on it." (negated). Only post_on_time_credit_a011cbd0 writes late_arrival_credit lines. False at opening: arrived 2026-07-07T13:12 against 12:10, no such line.
Edge 3: late_payment_charge -> refrigerant_allowance, value_input, gate l_bal, form state; policy_source "The late-payment charge is fixed only after every refrigerant line on an active member's call carries the member refrigerant allowance line owed on it." (affirmative). Only post_refrigerant_allowance_39aa6c52 writes member_refrigerant_allowance lines. False at opening: refrigerant line T0_l7 named by no allowance line.
Order: allowance and on-time credit commute (one hash-identified row each, additive balance updates, no position numbers; the credit reads the labor lines and is capped only by a balance far above it); then the charge; then the installment. Replayed both orders: identical hash.
Deletion sensitivity: skip the allowance -> late charge 5.42; skip the on-time credit -> 5.17; skip the late charge -> installment 142.70.
user_scenario names none of the three prerequisite problems; the tools validate nothing.

[Factor card]
Refrigerant allowance (baseline: Silver tier pounds 0.0 -> 0.00): consecutive_term_pounds 7 terms -> 0.5 lb (baseline 106.80); maintenance_count_window method: first enrolled 2020-06-15 (75 months) -> look back 24 months, 3 completed tune-ups (baseline current term only, 1 -> 133.50; near-miss: the 2025 visits belong to the previous term); maintenance_count_pounds 3 -> 0.5 lb (106.80); harbison_installation_pounds closed 2016-06-03, 124 months -> 0.2 lb (133.50); protection_contract_pounds W0 on the call's AC -> 0.3 lb (124.60); filter_subscription_pounds Pleated MERV 11 -> 0.2 lb (133.50). 1.7 lb x 89.00 = 151.30.
On-time credit (baseline: flat class credit 25.00): arrival_grace priority -> 10 min (baseline 15 -> 57 min -> x1 -> 83.90; near-miss: lateness against the class grace is under the 60-minute step); lateness_multiplier 62 min -> 1.5 (83.90); credit_basis method: active member, unit under contract -> 10 percent of repair labor 689.00 = 68.90, not below 25.00 (baseline flat 25.00 -> 52.50); comfort_call_addition no_cool without response guarantee -> 15.00 (103.35). 68.90 x 1.5 + 15 = 118.35.
Late-payment charge (baseline: grace 30, every started 30-day period, 1.5 percent, no relief -> 17.12): late_payment_grace 3 autopay drafts in 3 months -> 45 days (baseline 5.71; near-miss: the 2026-06-15 draft is exactly 3 months back); period_counting_convention method: 250.00 paid of 1312.20 charged (19 percent) -> periods run in full plus the running period as half = 1.5 (baseline started periods = 2 -> 5.71); late_payment_rate no late fee in 24 months -> 1.0 percent (baseline 6.42; near-miss: the 2024-08-31 late fee is 25 months back); tenure_relief enrolled 75 months -> 0.5 (baseline 8.56). 570.80 x 1% x 1.5 x 0.5 = 4.281 -> 4.28; no earlier late charge, so none already charged.
First installment (baseline: single payment 575.08): installment_count 7 terms -> 3 (baseline n 2 -> 289.68); balance_size_installments the July call's balance owing from its own lines 575.08 -> +1 (baseline n 3 -> 194.55; near-miss: the September duct-cleaning call still owes 530.10, and a reader who sums the customer's open lines across calls gets 1105.18 and wrongly takes +2); arrangement_minimum unit under contract -> 300 (baseline 750 -> one installment -> 575.08); up_front_amount method: autopay drafts in 12 months -> late charges alone 4.28 up front (baseline equal split -> 143.77). 4.28 + 142.70 = 146.98.

[Base-invariant card] Discount writes: member_active_on_posting (P0 active), courtesy_program_on_file (senior_65_plus; retired difficulty-wide by the courtesy policy's overwrite, kept as tolerated evidence), follow_up_within_window (repair on the diagnosing visit, day 0; just-before 2026-08-07 is day 31, at-boundary 2026-08-06 is day 30), within_guarantee (no earlier call on the record; vacuous; recall_of_ticket_id carried as the empty value of the record), one_on_time_credit (no on-time credit before the write); arrived_late retired by the on-time policy's overwrite. Charge write: charge_on_dispatched_call (completed), tuneup_class (Standard is tune-up bookable; no tune-up line is written), one_cancellation_fee (none on the call); late_charge_after_grace retired by the late-payment overwrite (90 > 45). Payment write: policy_scope.

[Business-object card] Ticket T0, Standard Service Call 2026-07-07 on the AC. Lines: diagnostic fee 89.00 offset by member rate 89.00; TXV parts 196.00 / labor 689.00 with member discounts 29.40 / 103.35; refrigerant 3.8 lb 338.20; card payment 250.00. Opening balance 840.45.

[World rows] customers C0 (senior); equipment E0a/E0b; install_projects I0 (closed 2016-06-03); warranty_contracts W0 (5-Year Labor on the AC, active, does not cover TXV or refrigerant) and its activation grant; plan_agreements P0 (Silver, monthly autopay, 7 terms, enrolled 2020-06-15); 54 dues rows from 2024-08 (one late fee 2024-08-31 paid 2024-09-03 by phone, every other month drafted by ACH autopay; dues balance 0.00); 5 visit rows; filter_subscriptions F0 (Pleated MERV 11); ticket T0 and 8 lines; a second, recent call T0b (Standard, 2026-09-28, whole-home duct cleaning on a poor-airflow call: diagnostic fee 89.00 offset by the member rate, duct cleaning 589.00 with the 10 percent Silver duct-cleaning discount 58.90, 530.10 owing, 7 days old, nothing missing and nothing past due) which every computation of this tree leaves out because each reads the July call alone. Silver has no response guarantee, so the late arrival creates no plan credit; no other category carries an open obligation.

[Persona design] Harold Kowalczyk, 71, retired machinist; volunteers the past-due notice, the July repair, the 250 dollars paid at the door and the wish to set up a payment arrangement and pay the first part by debit card; identity on request; agrees generically to corrections; pays the stated amount by card; ends after the confirmation number.

[Solution] find_customers -> verify -> reads (tickets, the customer's lines on both calls, equipment, agreement, visits, dues, contracts, claim entries, installation, filter) -> allowance 1.7 lb / 151.30 on T0_l7 -> on-time credit 118.35 on T0_l1 -> late charge 4.28 -> customer pays 146.98 by card. Closing balance 428.10.

[Revision log — round 2 (policy-task audit)]
F-G1: the late-payment rule promised "not yet charged" periods but compute charged every counted period. Compute now reads the posting date of the call's latest late-payment charge (LATEST), counts the periods as of that date with the same grace and convention, and charges only the difference; the rule and baseline paragraph state it ("Periods already charged are ..."). No effect on this world (no earlier charge).
F-G3: lateness_multiplier and tenure_relief relabelled parameter (they select numbers). New honest methods: on-time credit_basis (the credit is figured as a share of the call's repair labor lines for members, or as the flat class credit otherwise: a different amount algorithm reading different records) and late-payment period_counting_convention (periods counted as completed periods / completed plus a half running period / every started period — a day-count convention).
F-G4: charging_period_length (set by dues billing cadence) removed; the charging period is the fixed 30 days. The maintenance look-back is now set by how long the member has been enrolled (24 / 12 months / current term), not by billing cadence or auto-renew. filter_subscriber_installments replaced by balance_size_installments (the balance owing worked out from the invoice lines decides +2 / +1 / 0). The scope-restating "agreement active" conjunct removed from consecutive_term_pounds.
T0-F3: near-miss added to the installment computation (invoice charges 1312.20 vs balance owing 575.08 for the balance-size tier).
T0-F4 / O-G7: every cent rounding in the compute now adds a nudge of 0.000000001 before RND so binary-float ties round half up as the rules say; every recorded figure re-run through the gate's evaluator.
O0-2: the dues ledger is now seeded back to 2024-08, so the 24-month late-fee window rests on records (and carries a near-miss late fee 25 months back).
To keep the late-payment factors all load-bearing under the new convention, the July call moved from 2026-07-17 to 2026-07-07 (booked 2026-07-02): 90 days at frozen_time.
O-G6: compute_basis entries added for the allowance's lookup bindings. O-G3: the courtesy rule restates the repair-line courtesy terms instead of pointing back to superseded text.

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] From the published rules, tool schemas and finder outputs alone: the arrangement rule's sentence forces the late charge first; the late-payment rule's two sentences force the allowance and the on-time credit; each rule fixes its own amount, rounding and order; one reading only.


[Revision log — round 3 (policy-task audit revision_2)]
T0-F3: a genuine record-level near-miss now sits in the installment computation. The customer also has a recent duct-cleaning call (T0b, completed 2026-09-28) with 530.10 owing and not yet past due; the gold read now lists the customer's invoice lines across both calls (find_service_lines by customer), so the agent sees them. The balance-size rule reads "the call's charge lines, less its discount, coverage-credit and payment lines, plus its refund lines" — the July call only. A careless reader who adds the September call's open lines gets 1105.18 and the +2 tier (5 installments, first installment 4.28 + 114.16 = 118.44) instead of +1 (4 installments, 146.98). The September call owes nothing else (diagnostic fee fully offset by the Silver rate, technician on time, duct-cleaning discount posted, 7 days old) and seeds no obligation outside the tree. seed_consistency covers its ticket and four lines.
O-R2-2: the late-payment rule's started-period sentence now opens "Under the standard count, ...", and the conditional sentence reads "Which count applies depends on what the customer has paid toward the call: ... instead of the standard count; ... instead of the standard count; when nothing has been paid toward the call, the standard count applies." The unconditional reading (5.71 / 148.41) is no longer available from the words; the overwrite's replaced_by quotes the new sentence. Gold unchanged (4.28 / 146.98).
O-R2-1: every rule states the half-up tie-break in words ("An amount that falls exactly halfway between two cents is rounded up to the higher cent.").
O-R2-4 and the remaining lookup bindings: basis keys added (see task 1's log; charter-wide).
user_scenario: You are Harold Kowalczyk, 71, a retired tool-and-die machinist who lives at 3418 Riverglen Dr in Upper Arlington. You are calling Harbison Heating & Air because a past-due notice came in the mail for the air-conditioning repair they did at your house back in July: the technician replaced a valve on the outdoor unit and recharged it, and you put $250 on your card at the door that day. You meant to pay the rest and it slipped your mind while you were helping your daughter move. You are on a fixed income, so you would rather not pay the whole remaining bill at once: you want to set up a payment arrangement and make the first payment today on your debit card. You do not remember what is still owed and you expect the agent to tell you. When the agent asks who you are, you give the phone number on the account, 6145553271, and if they need one more detail your four-digit account PIN, 7340; if they ask for your address or email instead, it is 3418 Riverglen Dr and harold.kowalczyk@outlook.com. You do not know any account or reference numbers. If they ask about your Comfort Club membership, your filter deliveries or the protection plan on the air conditioner, you say you have all of those but they can see the details better than you can. Only if the agent asks whether the technician arrived on time do you say that he came in the early afternoon and you did not time it. If the agent tells you that something has to be added to or taken off the bill before the payment can be worked out, you tell them to go ahead and do whatever is right; you do not ask how much. You leave the number of payments and the size of the first one to the agent and do not ask for a different schedule. Once the agent tells you the amount of the first payment and hands you the payment step, you pay exactly that amount with your debit card, which is a card payment. When the payment goes through and you hear a confirmation number, you thank them, say you will watch for the next payments, and end the call without asking for anything else.
